subject_title: Organic Chemistry: Alkenes Preparation and Chemical Properties
raw_transcription: -> From Alcohols -> Acid catalyzed dehydration -> Alcohols on heating with conc. H2SO4 form Alkenes with the elimination one water molecule. Since a water molecule is eliminated from the Alcohol molecule in the presence of an acid this reaction is known as acidic dehydration of Alcohols -> This is also an example of beta-elimination reaction CH3 CH2 OH -- conc. H2SO4 --> CH2=CH2 + H2O Chemical properties -> They undergo addition reaction 1) Addition of H2 H2C=CH2 + H2 -- Ni --> H3C-CH3 ethene ethane 2) Addition of Halogen H2C=CH2 + Br2 -- CCl4 --> BrCH2-CH2Br ethene The reddish-orange colour of Bromine solution in CCl4 is discharged when Bromine adds up to an unsaturated site. Therefore this test is used as a test for unsaturation (presence of double or triple bond) in a organic compound. Q) Suggest a chemical test to distinguish between Ethane and Ethene 3) Addition of HX (hydrohalogenation) H2C=CH2 + HBr ---> CH3-CH2Br

nodes.title: Acidic Dehydration of Alcohols
nodes.explanation: Heating alcohols with concentrated H2SO4 eliminates a water molecule to form alkenes.

nodes.title: Beta-Elimination Reaction
nodes.explanation: A reaction mechanism where atoms or groups are removed from adjacent carbon atoms (alpha and beta) to form a multiple bond.

nodes.title: Addition Reactions of Alkenes
nodes.explanation: Chemical reactions characteristic of unsaturated alkenes where atoms add across the double bond.

nodes.title: Addition of Hydrogen (Hydrogenation)
nodes.explanation: Addition of H2 across an alkene double bond in the presence of a Nickel catalyst to produce an alkane.

nodes.title: Addition of Halogen (Halogenation)
nodes.explanation: Addition of Br2 in CCl4 to an alkene to produce a vicinal dibromide.

nodes.title: Test for Unsaturation
nodes.explanation: Discharge of the reddish-orange color of bromine solution in CCl4 upon addition to double or triple bonds.

nodes.title: Addition of HX (Hydrohalogenation)
nodes.explanation: Addition of hydrogen halide (e.g., HBr) across an alkene double bond to yield a haloalkane.

questions.question_text: What visual observation indicates a positive test for unsaturation when using bromine in CCl4?

options.text: Discharge of the reddish-orange color of bromine solution
Color change from clear to deep blue

questions.explanation: When bromine adds across a double or triple bond (unsaturated site), the reddish-orange color of the bromine solution in CCl4 is discharged.

questions.question_text: Which reagent and condition are used to convert ethanol to ethene via dehydration?
questions.explanation: Heating alcohols with concentrated H2SO4 causes elimination of a water molecule to yield an alkene.
